periods.analysis: Part I Crime Rate opened the arc at 28.6 per 1,000 residents, green against the <=30 target and a solid starting point for council reporting. The green result reflects consistent precinct-level follow-up on the Summer Safe Blocks plan, including evening foot posts in the Marina District, directed patrol on Airport Way, and cargo-theft checks with Port Police at Gates 4 and 3) Data quality looks dependable: the Records Unit closed the quarter with incident coding reconciled before the scorecard deadline, which matters for keeping this measure credible. I would frame this for council as safe, stable, and actively managed rather than as a finish line.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the weekly CompStat review and keep the same Tuesday data-lock schedule so departments can validate Part I coding before publication. Extend the Summer Safe Blocks tactics into fall weekends on the Harborwalk and Route 12 nightlife corridor, where visitor volume remains high after cruise season. Ask Patrol and IT to keep the RMS dashboard filter for airport, seaport, and downtown beats visible in the council packet so the green result has operational context.

periods.analysis: The rate improved to 28.2 per 1,000 residents, down 0.4 from 28.6, keeping Harborview comfortably green. That movement is especially encouraging because Q4 carries holiday retail pressure at Bayfront Mall, the Terminal Avenue outlets, and the airport parking decks. The Retail Theft Working Group appears to have helped, with loss-prevention liaisons, camera-share requests, and two-person bicycle patrols reducing repeat calls along Pier Market Row. From a scorecard standpoint, this is the kind of modest but real quarter-over-quarter movement we should call out before anyone assumes green means passive.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Retail Theft Working Group through January returns season, with weekly case packets from the top 15 repeat locations. Extend directed patrol windows at Bayfront Mall transit stops from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. on Fridays and Saturdays, using overtime already approved in the holiday deployment plan. Keep the Q4 data note in the council narrative: 28.2 per 1,000 residents, down 0.4, green, and supported by specific deployment choices.

periods.analysis: Q1 held the line at 28.1 per 1,000 residents, down another 0.1 from 28.2 and still green. The smaller movement is not a concern; winter quarters often show lower street activity but higher indoor theft reporting, so a steady green result is useful. Patrol Districts North and Central kept the burglary follow-up cadence in place, and the Crime Analysis Unit pushed repeat-address alerts for apartment garages on Maple, Larkin, and 6th. The story for council is continuity: we did not lose ground after the holiday improvement, and the reporting cycle stayed clean.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the repeat-address alert process and require precinct supervisors to document action taken on the top 10 locations by the second Monday of each month. Extend garage and storage-unit prevention visits to the Eastbank and Midtown TOD areas before spring leasing turns over. Keep the Records Unit’s 5-business-day coding review as a non-negotiable scorecard dependency so the 28.1 result remains auditable.

periods.analysis: The rate moved up to 28.6 per 1,000 residents, an increase of 0.5 from 28.1, but it remains green and below the <=30 target. This is the first uptick in the series, and it lines up with warmer-weather foot traffic, school-year transitions, and more airport passenger volume around spring travel. The operational watch item is theft from auto around the Convention Center garages and the South Ferry lots, where Crime Analysis flagged clustered weekend incidents. I would describe this as a manageable seasonal lift, not a trend break, provided we tighten the deployment plan now.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green performance by keeping the spring directed patrol plan active through the first two weeks of summer rather than ending it at Memorial Day. Extend license-plate-reader review and garage ambassador reporting at Convention Center Lots B, C, and D, with weekly feedback to Parking Operations. Add a council-facing note that the measure rose 0.5 to 28.6 per 1,000 residents but remains green, with theft-from-auto as the concrete watch item.

periods.analysis: Q3 rose again to 29.2 per 1,000 residents, up 0.6 from 28.6, still green but closer to the <=30 threshold than I would like. The two-quarter increase deserves a friendly nudge to the operating teams, particularly because summer festivals, cruise passengers, and late-night waterfront activity all add exposure. The Harbor Days detail, the Seaport Connector patrol car, and the youth violence interruption team kept calls from turning into a broader public-safety story, which is why the result stayed green. For council, the right message is: yes, green; also, we see the slope and are managing it before it becomes a yellow conversation.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the festival deployment template, including pre-event trespass checks, light-tower placement, and the joint police-fire command post for large waterfront weekends. Extend the Seaport Connector patrol from Thursday-Sunday to Wednesday-Sunday through the final cruise departures, with a specific focus on vehicle prowls and disorder hotspots. Ask the Crime Analysis Unit to provide a one-page Q2-to-Q3 bridge for the October performance meeting so the 0.6 increase is explained with locations, not anecdotes.

periods.analysis: Q4 improved sharply to 27.9 per 1,000 residents, down 1.3 from 29.2, returning the measure to its best position in this arc so far. That decline suggests the summer interventions were not just temporary optics; the follow-through into the holiday period mattered. Downtown emphasis patrols, coordinated port gate checks, and targeted retail theft warrants on the Bayfront list all contributed to a calmer quarter. This is a strong green result, and it gives council a clear example of Harborview using performance data early enough to change the next quarter’s outcome.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Bayfront repeat-offender case review as a standing monthly meeting, not a seasonal task force. Extend the downtown emphasis patrol playbook to the Central Station transit sheds during January and February, when commuter theft reports typically rebound. Capture the Q3-to-Q4 improvement, down 1.3 to 27.9 per 1,000 residents, in the year-end scorecard summary so departments get credit for the course correction.

periods.analysis: Q1 edged down again to 27.6 per 1,000 residents, a 0.3 improvement from 27.9 and another green quarter. This is the lowest value in the eight-quarter sequence to date, which is worth noting without sounding like we are declaring victory. The winter burglary prevention cohort in North Harbor, the hotel corridor liaison checks near the airport, and continued warrant service on repeat theft cases kept pressure on the right problem sets. The data story is also tidy: incident submissions were reconciled before the March close, so the performance packet can move on time.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the winter burglary cohort for one more quarter, especially the doorbell-camera outreach and property-manager email bulletins for asset clusters NH-14 through NH-19. Extend airport hotel corridor checks into the early-morning shuttle window, 4 a.m. to 7 a.m., when luggage and vehicle prowls are most preventable. Use the 27.6 per 1,000 residents result as a benchmark in the FY2027 budget discussion for preserving analyst capacity and targeted patrol flexibility.

periods.analysis: The most recent quantified result was 29.4 Part I crimes per 1,000 residents, an increase of 1.8 from 27.6 in the prior quarter—approximately a 6.5% rise. Although 29.4 remained within the prior threshold of 30 per 1,000, the increase reduced the remaining margin to 0.6 per 1,000, leaving performance vulnerable to a relatively small additional increase. The increase was associated with theft from auto and commercial burglary near spring events, ferry overflow parking, and construction staging areas around East Harbor redevelopment permits, indicating concentrated rather than broadly described crime pressures. The current Below Plan status, alongside the Below Plan Safe & Secure Neighborhoods objective, indicates that this earlier deterioration has progressed into a material public-safety performance gap. Current-period rate data are not available to quantify the size of the gap.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the core CompStat and directed-patrol model that kept the rate green, but add a 30-day sprint on theft from auto at South Ferry, Convention Center Lots B-D, and the East Harbor construction perimeter. Extend police-private security coordination to the three largest active redevelopment sites, requiring weekly incident logs from site managers and camera access contacts by close of business Friday. Bring a brief exception note to the next scorecard review: 29.4 per 1,000 residents, up 1.8, green, with a concrete July deployment plan so council sees management action before the line reaches yellow.

periods.analysis: The rate declined from 31.2 to 30.9 per 1,000 residents, an improvement, but remains above the lower-is-better target of 28. Earlier reporting identified theft from auto and commercial burglary as concentrated concerns.
periods.recommendations: Keep directed patrol and incident review focused on the previously identified locations; report whether the next period sustains the decline.
